$comment: Machine state for the player-value and reliability delivery programme. Orchestration only. It never carries repository, hosted, contract, scoring or product facts — those live in their own authorities and are read fresh. See docs/product/player-value-programme-controller.md and tests/documentation/playerValueProgrammeController.test.ts.

contractRunway.note: The repository's own position is deliberately absent; it is read from the authority named above, which on any branch already carries that branch's own claim. What is recorded here is every OTHER open branch that holds a number, so the next free one is this branch's position plus one plus the claims below. Two branches holding one number is the known failure this record exists to prevent, so a claim names an exact pull-request head and is invalid the moment the repository reaches it.

openPullRequestClassification.rationale: vNext Games information architecture. It branched before this programme's recent stages and carries a STALE copy of this controller (stage 1 complete, stages 2 and 3 empty, this classification list emptied). Its migration set and contract claim match the repository's own position, so it competes for no number. Because both sides edited the same controller lines the merge CONFLICTS rather than silently reverting, which is the safe failure; whoever merges it must keep the repository's stage records rather than the branch's. Not this programme's branch to push to.

stages.title: Reconcile the contract runway
acceptanceEvidence: Migration numbering is unambiguous: no two branches hold one number, and the runway records the number the other open migration branch must take.
Every open pull request is classified on its exact head, in this record.
The programme controller, its orchestration contract and its executable gate are on main, reachable from the root agent router.

The gate refuses a completion with no merge behind it, a completion ahead of its dependency, blank evidence, an unnamed blocker, two stages in flight, two branches on one number, an overtaken claim, a hole in the runway, an unclassified claimant, a draft called ready to merge, and copied prose — proven against deliberately broken states and against an empty runway.
main was green on the exact head before merge.

stages.title: Deploy the reminder delivery path
acceptanceEvidence: The scheduled job that invokes the sender exists and reports itself when unconfigured, rather than raising every five minutes.
The per-row dry-run gate can refuse. The defect was measured first: the claim overwrote the flag it then handed back, so the gate had never been able to say no.
A run ledger records the refusal the delivery ledger structurally cannot, because the deployment gate declines before any row is claimed.
The administrator health panel derives whether a sender is configured instead of stating a literal, and distinguishes an unknown scheduler from a missing secret.
pgTAP suite 262 (40 assertions) and the panel render suite both green on the exact merged head.

stages.title: Web push notifications
acceptanceEvidence: Push is a second channel through the existing ledger: one column on the existing row, so the once-per-action key is untouched and a player with both channels is told once.
The subscription row is the opt-in; there is no second boolean beside the email preference, and turning push off deletes the endpoint and the keys.

A disowned endpoint falls back to email without a fallback being written, because the channel is recomputed on every claim rather than fixed at scheduling. Demonstrated end to end on a disposable PostgreSQL.

RFC 8291 encryption reproduces, byte for byte, a body generated by an independent implementation of the same specification. Reversing the two public keys in the key derivation was tried against it and fails.

The service worker gained a fourth stated refusal: a push payload is read as three strings and one same-origin path, and can make a notification say something wrong but cannot make a tap leave this site.
The lock-screen wording carries no prediction, pick, score, rank, name, address or time of day, asserted against every event kind the taxonomy defines.
Each of the migration assertions was proved non-vacuous by restoring the defect it guards.

Review found two real defects and both were fixed with the case that catches them: a notification tap discarded every non-root target because the stored data object was passed where a string was expected, and the email fallback could reach a player who had switched email off. Each fix was proved by restoring the defect and watching the new case fail.

A push endpoint is chosen by a browser and posted to by a service role, so both the schema and the sender refuse an address literal, a host with no dot and the private suffixes, and the sender does not follow redirects. Deliberately not an origin allow-list: the suites check that the four real push services are still accepted.

The visual-contract suite failed once and was re-run once rather than explained away: this branch changes exactly one file under the rendered source tree, nothing imports it, and the same suite had passed on nine earlier heads of the branch. The re-run passed.
stages.blocker: No player can turn push on yet, and the blocker has NARROWED rather than cleared. Its first half is done: hosted Development now carries this migration, so the schema the switch needs exists. Its second half does not: the generated database types are still the ones produced before that rollout and contain no reference to the push surface at all, and every call from the application is checked against them, so the account surface still cannot offer a switch. One action remains, and it is smaller than the original: regenerate the types from Development and commit them. That needs a credential this repository holds as a secret and no agent session does — scripts/generate-database-types.mjs refuses without SUPABASE_DEV_DB_URL or SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, which is the correct refusal. The reminder stays executable: tests/vnext/notificationPreferences.test.tsx fails the moment the regenerated types know the save function, and its comment says what to build.

stages.title: Server-rendered invite metadata and dynamic share cards
acceptanceEvidence: An invite link rewrites to a build-derived join document that says it is an invitation; the document is taken from the Vite bundle asset, so it can never drift from index.html's hashed script and stylesheet tags.

The card is a pure function of the site and takes no invite code: contracts 152, 158 and 159 narrowed invite disclosure onto one rate-limited budget, and a crawler-fetched card carrying per-code content would be a fourth, unlimited door. A card that merely DIFFERED between a real and a guessed code would be a free validity oracle, so the suite asserts the arity (inviteShareCard.length === 1) rather than the wording.

robots.txt carries Disallow: /join/ and the invite document carries noindex, nofollow and emits no canonical or og:url. Each of the three disclosure guards was proved by removing what it guards and watching it fail.
Closes the crawlable half of SEC-001 and advances SEO-002, both recorded in docs/quality/risk-register.md.
No migration; the deployment contract is untouched at 217.

stages.title: Deterministic hostile scenario seed
acceptanceEvidence: Named scenarios seed the three hostile states the design rule names and the seed previously could not express: a guaranteed tie on the top total, entries that were never submitted, and a one-member and two-member pool.

The tie is created by construction — the best entry's predictions are copied onto the worst, so they must score identically — and verified through the real scoring pipeline rather than by any reimplementation of it.
Every guarantee was proved by removing it and watching the assertion fail, in four directions; an unrecognised scenario name refuses rather than falling back to the ordinary world.
The dry run ranks submitted entries only, matching what the database ranks from, after review found it would otherwise print a table the seeded app refuses to render.
The default scenario is byte-identical to the previous output, so nothing depending on the seed moved. No migration.

stages.title: Adversarial failure-mode tests
acceptanceEvidence: The adversarial question was where a binding product rule states a number nothing checks the code still honours, rather than adding volume to 239 test files that already cover failure, retry, timeout and conflict.
Found live: the design system requires a fifty-player pool before a percentile is shown, on a de-anonymisation and dignity rationale, while the implementation enforced twenty-five.
The boundary assertion could not have caught it, because it was written in terms of the constant under test; the guard now reads the number out of the authority and requires exactly one match.
Proved in four directions: the code diverging, the document's number gutted, the rule deleted from the document, and a second matching phrase added.

A second instance of the same fault was found and fixed while fixing the first: the controller's out-of-order case sourced its fixture from live data and stopped working once every dependency completed.
